scoreNote: Strong-adequate (4.5): grants that persuading an opponent is a strong test while arguing it is not the only one; two developed examples with analysis, controlled prose on a memorable First and Second skeleton.

sentences.text: An argument may sound perfect to us yet fail to move anyone who disagrees.
Some people argue that the best test of an argument is its ability to convince someone with an opposing viewpoint.
I agree that persuading an opponent is a strong test, but I do not believe it is the only measure of a good argument.

sections.role: Body 1 — Why persuading opponents is a strong test

sentences.text: First, convincing someone who disagrees is indeed a powerful test of an argument.
An opponent has every reason to resist, so persuading her shows the argument is truly strong.
For example, a lawyer who changes the mind of a doubting jury has clearly made a compelling case.
This shows that winning over a sceptic is a genuine sign of a sound argument.
Arguments that only please those who already agree may simply be flattering their beliefs.
Facing real opposition forces an argument to prove its true strength.
To this extent, persuading an opponent is a valuable test.

sections.role: Body 2 — Why it is not the only test

sentences.text: Second, however, the power to convince is not the only mark of a good argument.
Some true arguments fail to persuade people who are stubborn or closed-minded.
Consider a sound scientific argument that a person rejects simply because it offends her beliefs.
Such cases show that failing to convince does not always mean the argument is weak.
A good argument also depends on solid logic and reliable evidence, whether or not it persuades.
Skilled speakers can also persuade with clever tricks rather than genuine truth.
Persuasion, then, is one important test but not the only one.
In conclusion, convincing an opponent is a strong and revealing test of an argument.
But logic and evidence matter too, since true arguments do not always persuade.
The best arguments combine the power to persuade with sound reasoning and solid proof.
